summary: Describes private SIP extensions between proxies that support the PacketCable Distributed Call Signaling architecture. Telephone service providers need to exchange trusted information about customers and calls when operating across domains, and these extensions provide that.

eli5.summary: Cable phone companies pass calls to each other and need to share trusted facts about each caller. This note adds special message fields so they can do it safely.

questions: how do sip proxies exchange trusted caller information
subtitle: Five private SIP headers that let trusted proxies in a phone provider's network share billing, trace, operator and surveillance data.

tldr.problem: To run residential telephone service at very large scale across domains, trusted elements owned by different providers must exchange customer and billing information that ordinary SIP does not carry.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines private SIP headers (P-DCS-Trace-Party-ID, P-DCS-OSPS, P-DCS-Billing-Info, P-DCS-LAES, P-DCS-Redirect) that appear only inside a trust boundary and are removed before leaving it.
tldr.outcome: They are meant only for closed administrative domains or federations with agreed policies, and need IPsec or TLS plus mutual authentication. This RFC obsoletes RFC 3603.

today: RFC 5503 is an Informational RFC and replaces RFC 3603. The metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it, and the text restricts its use to closed administrative domains.

sections.title: Applicability and the Trust Boundary
sections.content:
These Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) extensions assume certain network topology, a link between SIP and lower layers, and transitive trust. The RFC says those assumptions are generally not applicable in the Internet as a whole. The headers are only for closed administrative domains, or federations of them with previously agreed-upon policies, as in the DCS architecture. Use elsewhere could leak sensitive or private information. Even the RFC 2119 words apply only within that scope.

The DCS architecture draws a trust boundary around systems the service provider owns or controls, such as proxies, bridge, voicemail and announcement servers. Customer premises equipment and third-party servers are outside. Billing and accounting data stays inside; endpoint identity may be shown to untrusted endpoints or withheld according to subscriber profiles.

A user agent (UA) may be inside or outside the boundary depending on its function, so the procedures are split into trusted and untrusted UAs, each for the client (UAC) and server (UAS) role. Proxies are described as originating (received the request from an untrusted endpoint), terminating (sends to an untrusted endpoint) or, for billing, tandem.

The RFC also defines a private-URL: a SIP URI generated by a proxy whose userinfo holds or points to information that must not leave the trusted domain, such as billing account numbers or surveillance parameters. It is either stored locally or encrypted with a key known only to the proxy, with a checksum to detect tampering.
sections.eli5: Think of a building with a locked staff area. Notes inside may mention things like who pays the bill, but those notes must be taken off before anything goes out to a visitor.

sections.title: Call Trace and Operator Services
sections.content:
P-DCS-Trace-Party-ID supports customer-originated trace, which lets a called party report obscene or harassing calls to law enforcement even if the caller asked for anonymity. An untrusted UAC puts the header in an INVITE, together with the Target-Dialog header from RFC 4538 to identify the call. The Request-URI uses userinfo call-trace. The header carries a name-addr for the remote endpoint and an optional timestamp parameter in NTP timestamp format. If the remote party is unknown, the UAC SHOULD use an anonymous URI such as sip:anonymous@anonymous.invalid. A trusted UAS records and reports the identity, then redirects the call with a 3xx response to an announcement server or the provider's business office. The header never appears in responses.

P-DCS-OSPS tells a UA to give special treatment to a call from a PSTN Operator Services Position System or an emergency (9-1-1) PSAP call. Its three values are BLV (busy line verification), EI (emergency interrupt) and RING (operator ringback). Only trusted UACs may send it; an untrusted source's header MUST be removed by a proxy or the request rejected with 403 (Forbidden). A UAS that accepts BLV sends an audio stream to the address in the SDP, and SHOULD NOT reject it for being busy or alert the user. An accepted RING makes the UAS perform operator ringback, for example a 3-second howling tone or a sustained ring.
sections.eli5: One label lets someone report a nasty prank call, and another lets a phone operator check a line or ring a phone in an emergency even when it is busy.

sections.title: Billing Information
sections.content:
Ordinary SIP identifiers are not enough for billing. The Call-ID is chosen by the originating user agent and may not be unique over time, billing data may differ for each call by the same user, and split charging can bill several parties. So P-DCS-Billing-Info carries billing data separately from the caller and callee identities. It is used only between proxies and trusted UAs and is never sent to an untrusted UA.

The header holds a Billing-Correlation-ID (BCID), a slash, and a Financial-Entity-ID (FEID), followed by optional parameters. The BCID is specified externally as a 24-byte structure and is encoded as a hexadecimal string of up to 48 characters. The FEID is an 8-byte structure encoded as up to 16 hex characters followed by @ and a domain name. Parameters are rksgroup (Record-Keeping server), charge, calling, called, routing, locroute and jip (jurisdiction information).

The originating proxy or trusted UAC MUST generate the BCID and put it in the initial INVITE or SUBSCRIBE, along with its FEID and RKS group, and any local number portability (LNP) routing numbers it obtained. The terminating side MUST include its own BCID and FEID in the first reliable 1xx (except 100) or 2xx response, and MAY change the charge value, for example for a toll-free call. For redirects and transfers, proxies hand out a private-URL that embeds the billing data and expires very shortly in the future, to stop the originator from reusing it for multiple calls.
sections.eli5: Each call gets a number that works like a receipt number, so the phone companies can match up all their records and decide who pays for which part.

sections.title: Lawful Intercept and Redirect Headers
sections.content:
The RFC notes that, per RFC 2804, the IETF supports documenting lawful intercept technology if it must be developed, and points readers to RFC 2804 for the privacy, security and complexity issues.

P-DCS-LAES carries what is needed for Lawfully Authorized Electronic Surveillance: the address and port of an Electronic Surveillance Delivery Function for a duplicate stream of event messages, optionally an address for call content, and optional bcid and cccid (call content channel identifier) parameters. P-DCS-Redirect carries the original called party, the redirecting entity and a count of redirections. In the RFC's example, when C forwards to D after A called B who forwarded to C, the count is 2. The RFC notes this overlaps with the History-Info header of RFC 4244 and is kept for backwards compatibility with existing implementations.

Both headers are used only between proxies and trusted UAs and MUST NOT be sent to or by untrusted parties. Whether they are present is controlled by legislation, regulation and court orders, which MUST be followed, so a SHOULD in these sections means either MUST or MUST NOT depending on the applicable orders. If the terminating equipment cannot do the surveillance, such as a voicemail server, the terminating side SHOULD ask the originating proxy to do it through a P-DCS-LAES header in the response.
sections.eli5: When a court order says a call may be listened to, these labels tell the phone equipment where to send a copy. The labels are never shown to ordinary customers.

sections.title: Security Requirements
sections.content:
Quality-of-service gate coordination, billing information and electronic surveillance information are all sensitive. They MUST be protected from eavesdropping and need integrity checking. The RFC says use of IPsec or TLS between proxies and trusted UAs is REQUIRED, and mutual authentication is also REQUIRED, both between proxies and between trusted UAs and proxies. It MAY be done with administratively pre-shared keys or through another trusted third party.

If IPsec is used, the security policies of the administrative domain, and all connections between domains in the federation, MUST define an interoperable set of options. A minimum mandatory-to-implement IPsec configuration is given by an external PacketCable security specification.

The IANA section registers the five header names and their parameters in the SIP Parameters registry, and marks the old key parameter of P-DCS-LAES as OBSOLETED.
sections.eli5: Because these notes are private, the companies must lock the pipes between their machines and check each other's identity every time.

sections.title: Changes since RFC 3603
sections.content:
This RFC replaces RFC 3603. The main changes listed are a timestamp parameter and Target-Dialog procedures for P-DCS-Trace-Party-ID, a jip parameter for P-DCS-Billing-Info, and BCID and cccid parameters for P-DCS-LAES. P-DCS-Billing-Info is applied to SUBSCRIBE and P-DCS-Redirect to REFER. The use of QoS authorization for content intercept is made optional, and PUBLISH and MESSAGE were added to the method applicability tables.

The P-DCS-LAES header here is not backwards compatible with RFC 3603. It adds the cccid parameter, deletes security key information and does not mandate the BCID.
sections.eli5: The first version had some gaps. This update adds a few new fields and drops a security-key field.

items.label: Busy line verification
items.desc: Only in an initial INVITE establishing a new dialog.

items.label: Emergency interrupt
items.desc: Only within a dialog established with BLV.

items.label: Operator ringback
items.desc: Only within a dialog established by a UAC to an operator or PSAP.
